title: Mount USB drive with write access for regular users
summary: By default, mounting a USB drive as root might restrict write access to other users. This command mounts the drive with specific options to allow regular users to write to it.
prerequisites: You know the device path (e.g., /dev/sdb1) and the mount point (e.g., /mnt/usb).

steps.explain: Mount the USB device with options that set the group to 'users' and file/directory masks to allow write access for group members. Replace <DEVICE> with your USB partition and <MOUNT_POINT> with the directory where you want to access the files.

placeholders.name: MOUNT_POINT
placeholders.description: The directory to mount the USB drive to

steps.expect: The command completes without error. You can now create files in <MOUNT_POINT> as a regular user.

warnings: Ensure the mount point directory exists before running the command.
If the file system is read-only (e.g., NTFS without proper drivers), this command will not enable writing.

rollback.explain: Unmount the drive to revert the changes.
